Article Title: ‘Came close at high speed’: What led to India-Pakistan naval collision at Arabian Sea
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Wednesday summoned Pakistan’s top diplomat in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over the “unacceptable and unprofessional conduct” of a Pakistani naval ship. .The incident took place on the evening of September 15, when a Pakistan Naval Ship came close to a frontline Indian Navy warship on a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea. The Pakistani vessel was travelling at high speed and manoeuvring in “unprofessional and unsafe manner,” sources said.No damage was reported in the incident.The MEA said the Pakistani vessel’s conduct was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991.“While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991,” the MEA said in a statement.The Pakistani Charge d’Affaires was advised to convey to the concerned authorities that all military units must exercise due care and follow relevant agreements between the two countries.“The Charge d'Affaires of Pakistan was advised to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities, the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents,” it said.India has also instructed its Charge d’Affaires in Islamabad to lodge a similar protest with Pakistan’s ministry of foreign affairs.
Article Summary: The incident took place on the evening of September 15, when a Pakistan Naval Ship came close to a frontline Indian Navy warship. The Pakistani vessel was travelling at high speed and manoeuvring in “unprofessional and unsafe manner,” sources said. No damage was reported in the incident.

Article Title: 'Conjecture and preconceived': SC refuses to rejig panel probing police action during CJP protest
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to reconstitute a five-member high-powered committee set up to probe alleged police excesses against student protesters in Delhi, saying that the committee was formed with the highest standards of fairness and transparency.This comes after a plea was filed in the apex court alleging that one of the members of the committee was a close friend of a high functionary who is involved in the matter.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that the allegations against the panel were based on “conjecture and preconceived notions” even before it had commenced its enquiry."We are not inclined to effect any alteration in the constitution of the Committee, particularly where the prayer for such reconstitution proceeds on nothing more than conjecture and preconceived notions, articulated even before the HPEC has embarked upon its enquiry," the bench said."With respect to the concerns voiced over the treatment of witnesses and of those who may wish to come forward before the HPEC to furnish their account and voice their grievances, we request the HPEC that such vulnerable witnesses be extended due protection and their identities be kept confidential and undisclosed," it added.The bench directed that Senior Advocate Monika Gusain, along with advocate C Solomon, shall assist it as a representative of the HPEC, and shall further act as an independent arbiter between the parties."Similarly, we also request the HPEC to appoint a member secretary at the earliest, so as to facilitate any such logistical or other secretarial assistance as the HPEC may require in the discharge of its functions," the bench said.Earlier, advocate Prashant Bhushan raised doubts over one of the members of the panel, who was a former DGP of a northeastern state, and said he was under a "conflict of interest" as he was a close friend of a high functionary who was likely to be under investigation.Bhushan's views were backed by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, however, opposed the reconstitution of the committee and urged the apex court to ignore such allegations.The apex court formed the HPEC, headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy, to examine allegations of police excesses against student protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest march on July 20 in Delhi and violence against police personnel.The committee comprises former Punjab and Haryana high court chief justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi high court judge Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP L R Bishnoi."This HPEC has been constituted bearing in mind a wide variety of considerations, including the individual expertise and experience of each of its members, as well as the diversity of the committee, among other factors," the bench had said.The July 20 march saw clashes between protesters and security personnel, who used lathis and teargas shells to disperse crowds.
Article Summary: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that the allegations against the panel were based on “conjecture and preconceived notions” This comes after a plea was filed alleging that one of the members of the committee was a close friend of a high functionary who is involved in the matter.

Article Title: India, Pakistani naval ships collide in international waters; MEA calls conduct 'unprofessional'
Article Text:
The ministry said the Pakistani Charge d’Affaires was advised to convey to the concerned authorities (file photo)

What the 1991 agreement says

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday summoned Pakistan’s top diplomat in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over the “unacceptable and unprofessional conduct” of Pakistani naval units that led to a collision with an Indian Navy vessel in international waters.“While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991,” the MEA said in a statement.The ministry said the Pakistani Charge d’Affaires was advised to convey to the concerned authorities that all military units must exercise due care and comply with relevant agreements between the two countries.“The Charge d'Affaires of Pakistan was advised to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities, the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents,” it said.The MEA also said India’s Charge d’Affaires in Islamabad had been instructed to lodge a similar protest with Pakistan’s ministry of foreign affairs.This is not the first time Indian and Pakistani ships have come into close contact in the Arabian Sea.In 2011, a diplomatic row had erupted over the MV Suez episode, then Navy chief Admiral Nirmal Verma said Pakistani warship PNS Babur had come “much closer” than was prudent, damaging a helicopter net on INS Godavari. He said the Indian crew had acted “very professionally” and stressed that “there are clear rules of navigation at sea”.The 1991 India-Pakistan agreement lays down rules for advance notice of major military exercises, manoeuvres and troop movements.Under the agreement, the land, naval and air forces of both countries are to avoid major exercises close to each other. If such exercises are conducted within specified areas, the main force cannot be directed towards the other side and there should be no logistical build-up close to it.For land forces, exercises involving a division or larger formation are restricted within 5 km of specified areas along the International Border, Line of Control and the area between the Manawar Tawi and Ravi rivers. The agreement also requires advance notice for division-level exercises in designated areas, corps-level exercises within 75 km, and all exercises above corps level regardless of distance.For naval forces, an exercise involving six or more destroyer- or frigate-sized ships crossing into the other country's EEZ is covered. Air-force exercises at regional command level or above also fall under the agreement.
Article Summary: India summoned Pakistan’s top diplomat in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over the ‘unacceptable and unprofessional conduct’ of Pakistani naval units. The 1991 India-Pakistan agreement lays down rules for advance notice of major military exercises, manoeuvres and troop movements.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Wednesday stepped up its attack against the Centre and accused it of "giving into" United States' demand to get rid of zero MDR and charge for UPI.In a social media post on X, senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh dubbed the government's decision to introduce merchant discount rate on UPI as "NOTA - Narendra's Ongoing Trump Appeasement" and alleged that the move was aimed at helping US card companies compete with UPI."Tomorrow, the US House of Representatives votes on a Bill that introduces 100% tariffs on India. The US Senate has already approved this draconian law. Meanwhile, the Trump regime has been cracking down on Indian immigrants and making tougher laws against them. H-1B visa costs have been increased and such holders could soon be deported immediately when out of a job. Such holders are mostly IT professionals," Jairam Ramesh said."Here, the Modi Govt has given into a US demand to get rid of zero MDR and charge for UPI. The US Trade Representative earlier this year criticized UPI for being free and having driven out Visa and Mastercard. Why 0.4% MDR? Is it because debit card MDR is also 0.4%? Is this being done to enable US card companies to compete with UPI?" he questioned.The Congress leader claimed that the estimated cost of running the entire UPI ecosystem is around Rs 20,000 crore annually, which he said is less than 10% of what the RBI has been transferring to the Union government in the past few years to show healthy public finances for the Modi government."Is this going to make UPI 'sustainable' as the Govt claims? The estimated cost of running the entire UPI ecosystem is around Rs 20,000 crore annually. This is less than 10% of what the RBI has been transferring to the Union Govt in the past few years so as to show healthy public finances for the Modi Govt," he said."The PM has redefined NOTA - Narendra's Ongoing Trump Appeasement," the Congress leader added.Jairam Ramesh's remarks came after the National Payments Corporation of India on Tuesday introduced a new MDR framework, under which UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, while consumers will continue to transact free of cost using UPI.The revised UPI MDR framework will come into effect from October 15, 2026, and will apply to select merchant transactions.
Article Summary: Senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh dubbed the government's decision to introduce merchant discount rate on UPI as "NOTA - Narendra's Ongoing Trump Appeasement" He alleged that the move was aimed at helping US card companies compete with UPI.

NEW DELHI: Suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Tuesday night and burnt down at least two houses, while security forces engaged them in an exchange of fireAccording to officials, large number of militants armed with sophisticated weapons attacked Chawangkining Naga village around 10.30pm, hours after two Kuki women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in neighbouring Tamenglong district.CRPF personnel deployed in the nearby area returned fire, triggering intermittent firing that continued for nearly six hours until around 4.30am on Wednesday."Intermittent firing was reported for nearly six hours till 4.30 am on Wednesday. Article Summary: Suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Tuesday night and burnt down at least two houses. The attack came hours after two Kuki-Zo women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in Tamenglong district.

Article Title: Chile, Bhutan show rabies can be beaten, but India’s 2030 target faces hurdles
Article Text:
India's huge burden of dog bites, uneven implementation of dog vaccination and population management programmes, and gaps in surveillance have been cited as key challenges in meeting its 2030 rabies elimination target. (Photo: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: While Chile and Bhutan have recently demonstrated that dog-mediated human rabies can be eliminated as a public health threat, India may struggle to meet its own 2030 elimination target, public health experts have warned. They cited the country’s huge burden of dog bites, uneven implementation of dog vaccination and population management programmes, and gaps in surveillance as key challenges.Chile recently became the first country in South America to receive World Health Organization validation for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies, after more than five decades without a human case transmitted by a dog. Bhutan became the first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to receive the same validation earlier this month.Both countries achieved the milestone through sustained dog vaccination, population management, surveillance, laboratory testing and access to timely post-exposure treatment, offering India a model but also highlighting the scale of effort required.The World Health Organization estimates that 9.1 million animal bites occur in India every year, with more than three-quarters caused by dogs. An Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Epidemiology estimate puts annual human rabies deaths at around 5,726.India’s National Action Plan for Dog-Mediated Rabies Elimination focuses on mass dog vaccination, population management, surveillance, public awareness and timely post-exposure treatment. However, experts said the challenge lies in translating these measures into sustained action across districts.“Achieving the 2030 target will be difficult, but possible with district-level planning and coordinated action. Annual vaccination of stray dogs, effective animal birth control and dedicated spaces for strays are essential. Simply capturing them does not solve the problem,” said an expert on condition of anonymity.Dr Anil Kumar Gupta of the Association for Prevention and Control of Rabies in India and the Indian Public Health Association said the target may not be realistic at the current pace. He stressed mass dog vaccination, population management, proper wound care and timely post-exposure vaccination, while also flagging concerns over counterfeit rabies vaccines. “Never ignore a bite, even a scratch or lick,” he said.Dr Sumit Mor, Consultant & Head, Trauma & Emergency, Aakash Healthcare, said India could draw important lessons from Chile and Bhutan. “India can learn from Chile and Bhutan that rabies elimination needs sustained action, not one-off campaigns. We need dog vaccination above 70% year after year, stronger sterilisation and surveillance, mandatory case reporting, and free, uninterrupted post-exposure prophylaxis at every primary health centre.With coordinated action and sustained political commitment, the 2030 target remains within reach,” he said.The anonymous expert also pointed to competing interests around rabies control, saying a sharp fall in dog bites could affect demand for anti-rabies vaccines and rabies immunoglobulin.
Article Summary: India's huge burden of dog bites, uneven implementation of dog vaccination and population management programmes cited as key challenges. Chile recently became the first country in South America to receive World Health Organization validation for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies. An Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Epidemiology estimate puts annual human rabies deaths at around 5,726.

Article Title: CDSCO flags 2 Pakistani creams over excess heavy metals
Article Text:
Drug regulator alerts on unauthorised Pakistani whitening creams sale in India. (Photo: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has warned consumers against using two imported cosmetic creams after testing found them to be unauthorised for sale in India and containing excessive levels of heavy metals that may pose health risks.The cosmetics division of CDSCO has named Goree Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, both labelled as “Made in Pakistan”, in a public health alert dated September 8. The regulator said neither product had been issued a registration certificate by the competent authority for import and sale in India.CDSCO said laboratory testing and analysis had verified that the products were unauthorised and contained heavy metals beyond specified limits, which could cause toxic effects.The regulator has advised consumers not to buy or use the two products, or similarly named products if already purchased. It has also asked sellers, distributors and other establishments not to sell, distribute or advertise them. Regulatory enforcement units have been directed to ensure that the products are not sold in their jurisdictions.CDSCO said consumers should buy only authorised cosmetics carrying details such as the manufacturing licence number, manufacturer’s details, batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates, and, in the case of imported cosmetics, the registration number.The alert comes under the regulatory framework of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Cosmetics Rules, 2020. CDSCO said cosmetic manufacturing for sale requires a licence from the State Licensing Authority, while imported cosmetics must be registered with the Central Licensing Authority.
Article Summary: Goree Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, both labelled as “Made in Pakistan’, have been named in a public health alert. The regulator said neither product had been issued a registration certificate by the competent authority for import and sale in India.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's public event outside London's iconic Shard skyscraper was cancelled after the Metropolitan Police raised concerns over crowd safety.Hundreds of fans had gathered at the venue, with several waiting for hours to see the actor-turned-politician. His office said earlier that the delegation had signed multiple memoranda of understanding involving investments worth around Rs 12,300 crore during the visit.The investment agreements are part of the state's effort to position Tamil Nadu as a leading advanced manufacturing and technology hub in Asia. Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
Article Text:
Earlier, the Bombay HC ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Salian's death.

Bombay HC orders CBI probe

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty , Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Earlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.
Article Summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian. No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.

Article Title: Bangladesh PM was invited for Brics meet and bilateral visit: Govt
Article Text:
Tarique Rahman

NEW DELHI: Govt reiterated Tuesday that it had invited Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman for both Brics and a bilateral visit. In a letter dated July 14, accessed by TOI, PM Narendra Modi had invited Rahman for the Brics summit in his capacity as Bimstec chair and said his participation would "greatly enrich the deliberations".After Rahman's swearing-in as PM, Modi had invited him for a bilateral visit. Dhaka, however, pulled out of talks for finalisation of the visit dates, apparently because of the lack of any firm commitment from India on ex-PM Sheikh Hasina's extradition.MEA was responding to Dhaka's claim that India had invited the Bimstec chair and not Rahman. "I have said this before as well, we had invited the PM of Bangladesh on a bilateral visit. Subsequently, he was invited for Brics summit as chair of Bimstec. So, he had received two invitations, one on the bilateral side and the other for Brics," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.Modi had also said in his letter that this year's summit was of special significance as it marked 20 years of formal establishment of Brics.

Article Title: Sanjukta Parashar first woman to head CRPF’s CoBRA commando unit
Article Text:
Sanjukta Parashar

Studied at DU, JNU

Parashar posting part of CRPF’s push to put women in lead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: IPS officer Sanjukta Parashar, called the ‘Iron Lady of Assam’, has become the first woman officer to lead CRPF ’s jungle warfare commando unit, CoBRA.Parashar, a 2006-batch officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre, earned the moniker of Iron Lady after leading the crackdown against militant outfit National Democratic Front of Bodoland in 2013-14 as the then Sonitpur SP.Parashar, who is from Assam, has served both in her cadre as well as in NIA, specialising in key counter-terror investigations. She was heading the CID wing of Assam Police before being appointed IG, CoBRA.She will head CoBRA at a time when the force is engaged in holding and securing large forest areas, mostly in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, reclaimed from Naxals. These operations played a key role in almost eliminating Left-wing extremism in the country by March 2026.Two battalions of the force are also posted in Manipur, which has been witnessing intermittent violence fuelled by ethnic tensions.Parashar’s appointment as IG, CoBRA is part of a larger push by CRPF to place its women officers in lead roles, including ones that are operations- and combat-heavy.“Women are heading sectors like Jammu, CoBRA, Rapid Action Force, North East, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh as IG,” a CRPF officer told TOI.A few days ago, A Vijaya Laxmi, a 2006-batch IPS officer, was posted as IG, Jammu, a sensitive sector. Nitu D Bhattacharya heads MP sector as IG and oversaw the end of Naxalism in Balaghat. Kavita Jalan, an Odisha cadre IPS officer, is heading the North East sector that includes the whole of Meghalaya and parts of Assam. Archana Shivhare, a Gujarat cadre IPS officer, is IG, Rajasthan.RAF is also led by officer Seema Dhundia, inducted in the CRPF in 1987 as part of the first batch of female officers.Parashar had, at the start of her career as an assistant commandant, handled clashes between Bodos and illegal Bangladeshi immigrants. As Sonitpur SP, she led a crackdown on NDFB, leading to the killing of 16 militants and the arrest of 64 others. Her picture leading an operation with an AK-47 in her hand earned her the title ‘Iron Lady of Assam’, as well as death threats from Bodo militants.
Article Summary: IPS officer Sanjukta Parashar has become the first woman officer to lead CRPF’s jungle warfare commando unit, CoBRA. She earned the moniker of Iron Lady after leading the crackdown against militant outfit National Democratic Front of Bodoland in 2013-14 as the then Sonitpur SP.

Article Title: How fish has BJP's plate full in West Bengal
Article Text:
Bengal CM prayed at Kalighat temple and had fish-basanti pulao prasad.

From Liluah to Kalighat

Dhirendra Shastri on Durga Puja.

BJP pushback

BJP dismissed all anxieties over Durga Puja.

The not-so-new ‘maach-bhaat’ row

The Bengal and Bengali dilemma for Suvendu

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The larger question for BJP

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari last week offered prayers at the Kalighat Temple on the occasion of 'Kaushiki Amavasya' and partook of a traditional bhog that included fish and 'basanti pulao'. Interestingly, the timing of the visit gave the ritual a political context.The meal came amid a political controversy over Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's recent appeal to Bengali Hindus to refrain from eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja. As expected, the remarks kicked up a political storm, forcing the BJP’s Bengal unit to publicly distinguish itself from Dhirendra Shastri’s position on food.Chief minister Adhikari, who had shared a stage with Shastri earlier this month and invited him to establish a centre in Bengal, then got into the balancing act.“A religious figure is entitled to express his opinion, but whether people accept it or not is a personal matter,” the chief minister said after his Kalighat visit.Adhikari also referred to his own practices, saying he follows a sattvik diet on Ashtami and during Kartik, while accepting fish offered to Goddess Kali as bhog and goat meat as prasad."A saint or a religious leader is entitled to express their opinion. People may choose to accept it or not. On Mahashtami, when I worship Maa Durga, I consume sattvik food. During the month of Kartik also, I consume sattvik food. At the same time, as a Bengali, I accept the bhog offered to Maa with fish. I also accept the prasad of goat sacrifice. Today, whatever was offered to Maa in the afternoon, the temple priests gave me the same. There was fish head and fried fish, along with basanti pulao," he said.All this began on September 4, when Adhikari shared the stage with Shastri at a Hanumant Katha programme at the Liluah Workshop Ground in Howrah.Addressing Shastri, Adhikari said: "Baba Maharaj Ji, please open a centre here. There should also be a Bageshwar Dham centre. This is the land of saints and of spiritual awakening."Two days later, on September 6, Shastri appealed to Hindus in Bengal not to sell, cook or eat non-vegetarian food near Durga Puja idols during Navratri. He described those consuming such food as "pakhandi" and called for opposition to the practice."I am appealing to the Hindus of Bengal, that during Navratri, even if you don't keep the idols of the Goddess, do not sell or consume non-veg near the idols. I do not like it when dirty non-vegetarian food is eaten during Durga Puja and at gatherings linked to the festivities. I want the Hindus of Kolkata to awaken and boycott such people. These people cannot be considered religious; they are pakhandi (hypocrites). Wake up and expel those people," he appealed.The remarks triggered criticism from the opposition and prompted the Bengal BJP to distance itself from the dietary prescription.State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya said no one could decide what Bengalis should eat."How can Bengalis not have fish and meat?" he said, adding that people in Bengal would continue with their traditional food practices. He also invoked Swami Vivekananda while defending the consumption of meat and fish in Bengal’s religious traditions.Other BJP leaders, including Dilip Ghosh, also said food choices were a matter of personal preference and referred to the place of meat in some Bengali religious traditions.The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) also found itself navigating the controversy following statements made during an interactive session with Kolkata puja organizers. Swami Nirgunananda, a member of the VHP's central advisory council, had suggested that non-vegetarian food stalls be kept away from the immediate area around Durga idols and situated in designated spaces outside pandals to maintain sanctity and cleanliness.When his comments were interpreted as an official organisational diktat restricting meat sales, VHP International president Alok Kumar issued a formal clarification. "Vishva Hindu Parishad has not issued any directions regarding the arrangements at Durga Puja pandals... worship of the Goddess should take place according to tradition and the atmosphere should be one of love and devotion," it said.The Kalighat temple is associated with Bengal's 'Shakta' tradition, in which offerings can include fish and meat. The bhog included several varieties of fish, along with other vegetarian dishes and goat meat.That tradition sits somewhat differently from the vegetarian dietary practices associated with Navratri in several parts of north and west India.The controversy over Shastri's remarks comes months after fish and meat had already become part of the BJP-TMC contest over Bengali identity during the assembly election campaign.Mamata Banerjee repeatedly alleged during the campaign that a BJP government would restrict what Bengalis could eat. At a rally in Purulia on March 29, she said: "BJP says can't eat fish, meat, eggs." She subsequently argued that restrictions on meat and fish sales in some BJP-ruled states showed what could lie ahead for Bengal.The issue became prominent enough for senior BJP leaders to address it directly. Amit Shah clarified that "consumption of fish, eggs will not be stopped" if the BJP came to power in Bengal, calling Mamata's claim a rumour.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also sought to engage with the issue, though from a different direction. At a rally in Haldia, he spoke about Bengal's fish production and said the state could become self-sufficient in fish under a BJP government. "In 15 years, TMC couldn't even give you fish. We created a separate ministry for fisheries," he said, contrasting Bengal's production with that of Bihar and Assam.The BJP’s campaign also included more visible efforts to counter the perception that it was opposed to Bengali food habits. Leaders publicly ate fish and meat, while BJP candidates and workers used fish in campaign imagery. On Poila Boishakh, TMC organised a "Maach-Bhaat-e-Bangali" procession, alleging that the BJP would impose restrictions on fish and meat.The argument did not remain confined to the two parties. TMC leaders presented food as part of the broader question of Bengali identity. BJP leaders, in turn, sought to emphasise that dietary choices would remain a matter of personal freedom.Months after the BJP swept Bengal in assembly elections, the opposition has sought to use the same "outsider" charge to try and alienate the saffron party from the voters. Congress filed a police complaint against Shastri, alleging that his comments hurt Bengali sentiments, while invoking the “outsider” argument that the TMC had used against the BJP during the election. Congress’s complaint described his remarks as an affront to Bengali traditions and social harmony.The TMC, which had made fish and meat part of its cultural-identity campaign against the BJP, is also again using the remark against the party.As CM, however, Adhikari has also taken a position on protests against Shastri.On September 10, he directed the Kolkata Police commissioner to arrest those who allegedly burnt Shastri’s photographs during a protest in Bhawanipur. "Not in Bengal," he said, making clear that burning photographs as a form of protest would not be tolerated.The move has produced another political contest. Congress has criticised the arrests and accused the government of protecting Shastri while acting against those protesting his remarks. One Congress leader, Atanu Das, was subsequently arrested.The recent row has brought an old question back for the BJP in Bengal: how does the party's Hindu politics sit with the state's own traditions?Bengal has a strong Shakta tradition, centred on Kali and Durga. In this tradition, the line between what is considered religious and what is considered non-vegetarian is not always drawn in the same way as it is in northern/western India. Fish, and in some places meat, can be part of offerings and rituals.That makes food an unusually sensitive issue in Bengal. And for many Bengalis, it is tied to family customs, festivals and a sense of what is distinctly 'Bengali'.Suvendu Adhikari is leading the first BJP government in Bengal. For now, he might be able to shut down critics by consuming fish bhog at Kalighat. But it will be interesting to see how he manages BJP's national Hindu politics in Bengal while also balancing the "Bengaliness".
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari last week offered prayers at the Kalighat Temple and partook of a traditional bhog that included fish and 'basanti pulao' The meal came amid a political controversy over Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's recent appeal to Bengali Hindus to refrain from eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja.

A case was filed under UAPA. The matter was heard across multiple courts; even in Feb 2026, the Supreme Court rejected Umar Khalid’s bail plea. Look at the sympathy Congress party harbours for the very same Umar Khalid.”Patra also attacked Congress party over its meetings with Yasin Malik, alleging the party had reduced itself to “appeasement”.

NEW DELHI: For 15 days, Sunaina Devi (55) survived on river water and the fragile shelter of a half-submerged thatched hut, after being swept 50km downstream by the monsoon-swollen Ganga. She was found alive Monday by fishermen who heard her cries.Devi, from Kapurpatti village in Bihar's Buxar district, had gone to bathe on Aug 30 when the current pulled her under. Her son, Govinda Gond, filed a missing person report at Itarhi police station. Her family did not know she had drifted across the state border into Chain Chhapra village in UP's Ballia, on the other side of the river, soon after falling in.In Chain Chhapra, Devi managed to grab an abandoned hut in a field and pull herself up. Surrounded by floodwater, she survived by drinking from the same Ganga that had nearly drowned her.On Monday she collapsed and slipped once again into floodwater. Mallah fishermen in boats heard her chants of "Shivguru-Sh-ivguru", spotted her behind sarpat grass and pulled her aboard.Hunger strike studies in British Medical Journal say with water intake, the body can survive without food for 21 to 40 days."It was miraculous," Haldi SHO Rajiv Kumar Rai told TOI. Police gave her food and water and determined her identity.The family had feared the worst. "There was no update for so many days we genuinely thought we'd lost her," Govinda said.Police said relatives broke down in tears when they saw her. "They were not expecting to find her alive. The reunion was emotional and raw," Rai said.Her husband, Janardhan, a farmer, told TOI, "Deep down, there was still a flickering hope."Devi is still dazed. "It feels like my mind stops at one place. It was very difficult to be alone for so many days. I didn't know I had such strength in me," she says.Her family says she remains weak. Doctors expect the disorientation to ease in a few days.
Article Summary: Sunaina Devi (55) survived on river water and the fragile shelter of a half- submerged thatched hut. She was found alive Monday by fishermen who heard her cries. Devi, from Kapurpatti village in Bihar's Buxar district, had gone to bathe on Aug 30.

Article Title: Enforce speed curb device norms: SC to govts
Article Text: New Delhi: More than a decade after govt mandated installation of speed limiting devices or speed limiting functions in all public transport vehicles, enforcement remains lax, and Supreme Court Tuesday directed Centre, states and UTs to ensure compliance.Rule 118 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules provides for speed governors, and SC had passed various orders for installation of speed limiting devices. Though the SC committee on road safety had written to principal secretaries, transport secretaries and transport commissioners of all states and UTs in this regard, it was not implemented.Taking exception, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said the law had been framed by Centre and govt had to take steps to implement the statutory provision."Why does govt need directions from the court? These are statutory provisions and rules," the bench said.

Article Title: Multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests, better centres top reform wish list

NEW DELHI: A single bad day should not decide a student's future - and a poorly equipped examination centre should not ruin it. These concerns feature in thousands of suggestions received by the high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's examination system.The panel, led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, has been consulting stakeholders ahead of its next meeting, scheduled after the Brics summit. It will begin examining reform proposals, sources said.Constituted amid paper leaks, cancelled tests and infrastructure failures, the task force is examining examination security, technology, infrastructure, accessibility, student well-being and testing-agency reforms. Suggestions invited from citizens until Sept 13 will be compiled into a detailed report. A prominent demand is to give candidates multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests.Manojranjan Nayak, founder-president of Siksha 'O' Anusandhan, a deemed-to-be university, said: "Examination reform must move beyond making a flawed system more efficient. Multiple attempts can reduce the disproportionate cost of one bad day, but they should be combined with secure, accessible and uniformly equipped centres, transparent evaluation and greater weight for sustained learning.Technology can improve reliability, but it must not create a new divide between candidates with different levels of digital access. The real test of reform is whether every student, regardless of geography or income, gets a fair and dignified opportunity to demonstrate ability."Poor infrastructure at testing centres is another concern. Examinations at a Jaipur centre were disrupted by power failures on two consecutive days, affecting candidates and raising questions about how centres are selected and monitored.“For a young candidate, exam day carries years of preparation and the hopes of an entire family. If an examination is disrupted because the centre loses power or connectivity, it is not a small technical failure; it is the candidate who pays the price,” said Ashish Mittal, founder and managing director of Innovatiview.“That is why India needs Adarsh Pariksha Kendras, where reliable power, secure internet, tested computers, biometric verification and CCTV are basic standards, not last-minute arrangements. Every candidate deserves a fair examination in a centre that will not fail them,” he added.The issue is more urgent as agencies expand computer-based testing. The National Testing Agency has written to education ministry organisations seeking suitable centres. At its request, the All India Council for Technical Education has asked government technical institutions for details of computers, internet connectivity, power backup, CCTV and vacant spaces that could become standard testing centres.The government is identifying more public institutions to host entrance examinations from the next academic cycle, reducing dependence on private centres and building a more reliable national testing network.
Article Summary: High-powered task force set up to overhaul India's examination system. Panel, led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, has been consulting stakeholders. It is examining examination security, technology, infrastructure, accessibility, student well-being and testing agency reforms.

Article Title: Balakrishnan panel unlikely to propose inclusion of converts in SC list

NEW DELHI: A special panel may recommend to the govt that status quo should be maintained on the definition of Scheduled Castes, as laid down by the Presidential (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, and not expanded to bring in Dalit converts to Islam and Christianity.The commission of inquiry, headed by former Chief Justice of India KG Balakrishnan, has been mandated to investigate if status of Scheduled Castes can be extended to persons who have converted to religions other than those eligible for it - popularly known as "Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam".The 1950 Presidential Order states that only persons belonging to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism can be members of Scheduled Castes.The vexed issue has been pending before Supreme Court for over 20 years in which "Dalit converts" have demanded that they be included in the Scheduled Castes' list.Reports of the past commissions - Kaka Kalelkar, Sachar and Rangnath Misra - on the tricky issue, and the stand taken by National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) over the years have provided the background material for research. A 1911 book by a Christian missionary has also been relied upon.While Sachar did not recommend the Scheduled Castes status for religious converts, Misra panel did ask for the Scheduled Castes' list to be made religion-neutral. Its recommendation was apparently not accepted by govt because the panel did not conduct a study to reach its conclusion. Given the inputs, the commission may recommend that the present arrangement on eligibility for inclusion in Scheduled Castes' list should stay. Besides, there is also a lack of clarity on which of the religious converts were formerly members of Scheduled Castes, sources said.Pending for over two decades, the demand of religious converts to be included in Scheduled Castes' list has become controversial because of its political dimensions. Existing Dalit communities are often found to oppose fresh inclusions in Scheduled Castes' list, arguing that such a move will increase the number of claimants for job and educational reservations.BJP argues that making Scheduled Castes status religion-neutral will encourage religious conversions.
Article Summary: The 1950 Presidential Order states that only persons belonging to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism can be members of Scheduled Castes. The vexed issue has been pending before Supreme Court for over 20 years in which "Dalit converts" have demanded that they be included in the list. Existing Dalit communities often found to oppose fresh inclusions.

MUMBAI: The Foundation for Aviation Safety (FAS), a US aviation safety group, has written to India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), questioning why it has not issued interim safety recommendations for the Boeing 787 fleet, despite holding evidence of chronic system failures on the aircraft involved in last year’s Ahmedabad crash, which killed 260 people.Over the past year, FAS said it had received more than 100 non-public documents specific to the crashed Air India 171 aircraft (VT-ANB). FAS sent these documents to AAIB via a UK AAIB expert.“The documents are vital to reconstructing the operational history of the doomed airplane. These documents explicitly detail chronic, systemic aircraft failures involving the airplane’s electrical, electronic, and/or flight computer systems,” said Ed Pierson, FAS executive director, in an email to AAIB director general on Aug 29. “By actively withholding this information from public announcements, the AAIB is failing its primary objective, the prevention of future accidents through timely, transparent safety manager at Boeing’s Renton 737 factory, raised internal warnings about overworked, error-prone production teams that he says went unheeded. He later founded FAS, which came into prominence for its work scrutinising Boeing’s manufacturing and safety practices in the aftermath of the 737 MAX crashes, and disclosures.Most critically, despite being in possession of evidence pointing to chronic and dangerous system failures, AAIB has issued zero interim safety recommendations or warnings to the global aviation community,” it added.Pierson, a former senior manager at Boeing’s Renton 737 factory, raised internal warnings about overworked, error-prone production teams that he says went unheeded. He later founded FAS, which came into prominence for its work scrutinising Boeing’s manufacturing and safety practices in the aftermath of the 737 MAX crashes, and has since been pressing AAIB on the AI171 investigation.In an Aug 21 letter, FAS had asked to be formally recognised as a stakeholder in the investigation and for its technical findings to be included in the investigation record. AAIB’s Aug 26 reply confirmed it received the documents via a UK AAIB expert on June 10 and that its investigation team had examined them, adding that the probe followed fair and impartial practices under the relevant regulations. AAIB did not respond to FAS’s Aug 28 letter, which alleged the agency was suppressing vital B787 safety information.AAIB told TOI, “A common update/report will be published by the AAIB.”FAS first outlined the documents’ contents in a Jan presentation to the US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. Pierson told TOI the crashed aircraft’s records showed recurring failures in its Electrical Wiring Interconnection System (EWIS).It’s the network of all wires, cables and connectors distributing electricity, data and signals through the aircraft. The 787’s EWIS spans over 150 km of wiring, more than 3,500 connectors and 40,000 cable segments. Aircraft wiring was once treated as a minor component, but after the 1996 TWA B747 and 1998 SwissAir MD-11 crashes killed a combined 529 people, EWIS emerged as a distinct, critical aircraft system on a par with engines or fuel systems. The FAA formally codified EWIS regulations in 2007.“What I do know is that VT-ANB had plenty of EWIS failures,” Pierson said, citing the non-public documents. “It also had primary power distribution failures, not just EWIS, but actual power generation, stable, high-quality electrical power. It had lots of problems with that. It had all those other issues: open circuits, short circuits, burning, arcing, fire, etc.” He said problems could arise from wiring routed too close together, chafing against sharp edges, or improper bonding and grounding, leading to electricity going places it’s not supposed to go. “You can have a lot of issues with EWIS. EWIS has been identified as a causal factor in many accidents,” Pierson said.Among the documents sent to AAIB is one detailing a 2022 incident when VT-ANB, flying into Frankfurt, suffered multi-system failures on both sides of the aircraft. On landing, the P100 primary power panel was found burning, producing “12 pages of aircraft system faults”.“That’s what’s called a compound emergency... What this document shows is that the fleet is susceptible to this kind of failure, because it happened on this plane,” he said.The panel had to be replaced, a repair he compared to accessing “your circuit breaker panel at home... on steroids,” requiring technicians to cut and splice wires and reintegrate them into the system. He said the incident shows that VT-ANB itself had a history of such failures and alleged that the wider 787 fleet “is susceptible to this kind of failure”.
Article Summary: The Foundation for Aviation Safety (FAS), a US aviation safety group, has written to India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau. FAS said it had received more than 100 non-public documents specific to the crashed Air India 171 aircraft (VT-ANB)

Article Title: DRDO has developed indigenous GaN tech for next-gen radars, electronic warfare: Def min report
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Defence Research and Development Organisation ( DRDO ) has successfully demonstrated and implemented indigenous Gallium Nitride Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (GaN MMIC) Technology for high-frequency defence systems that can support next-generation radars and electronic warfare systems, the defence ministry's latest annual report for 2025-26 has revealed.After working for years, DRDO developed the GaN MMIC technology in 2024 and helped India quietly entered an elite club of seven countries — US, Russia, France, Germany, South Korea, China — after the country was reportedly denied the technology by a western nation during the negotiations for a major fighter jet deal.In layman’s language, a GaN MMIC is a tiny, super-powerful computer chip built on a special chemical material that handles extremely high-frequency wireless signals without melting. It’s an all-in-one chip that combines tiny parts—like transistors, resistors, and capacitors—onto a single piece of material to manage invisible wireless waves (microwaves).“DRDO has worked on cutting-edge defence technology and it has now matured,” a defence source told TOI. GaN is a material with exceptional thermal and electrical properties, making it critical for advanced defence applications such as sensors, radars, satellites, and missiles.“A single indigenous GaN chip, measuring 3.5 x 3 mm can deliver up to 30 watts of power and operate at speeds 300 times faster than silicon. Indigenous GaN MMIC technology for application upto X band has been successfully demonstrated and implemented,” the ministry’s report said.“Indigenously fabricated S-band GaN High Electron-Mobility power bars, power amplifier, low noise amplifier and switch MMICs have been designed, fabricated and demonstrated,” the report added.Meena Mishra, director of DRDO’s Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL) led her team that is behind the successful development of indigenous GaN MMIC technology. Over the course of more than 34 years, Meena has made significant contributions to semiconductor research and has been instrumental in the indigenous development of GaAs and GaN-based MMIC technologies for strategic applications. Her research expertise spans GaAs MESFET-based MMICs, GaAs-based digital integrated circuits, and the modeling, characterisation, and design of high-frequency devices using GaAs and GaN technologies.With rising demands for lighter and more compact power supplies in future combat systems, GaN/SiC technology provides a vital foundation for communications, intelligence, reconnaissance, and unmanned systems for both military and commercial sectors, including electric vehicles and renewable energy.
Article Summary: Defence Research and Development Organisation ( DRDO) has successfully demonstrated and implemented indigenous Gallium Nitride Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (GaN MMIC) Technology for high-frequency defence systems. The technology can support next-generation radars and electronic warfare systems. After working for years, DRDO developed the GaNMMIC technology in 2024.

Wagle has estimated that Nepal may need as much as $5 billion for rebuilding and rehabilitation. “We will require much less than what we needed for the 2015 earthquake. Loss and damage is being assessed,” he said.He has also said govt has enough resources for immediate rescue and relief but will need substantial outside support for reconstruction. “The next phase will focus on early recovery, including temporary shelters and cash-for-work programmes,” Wagle said.“This will be followed by the daunting task of reconstruction.”India has already emerged as one of Nepal’s key partners in the immediate response, sending nearly 50 tonnes of relief material, including medicines, temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits and solar lamps, while Indian teams also joined specialised rescue efforts in flood-hit areas. New Delhi later approved export of up to 654MW of electricity for 18 hours a day until Dec 31 after damage to Nepal’s hydropower network forced Kathmandu to halt power exports and turn to imports.India has also begun supplying Bailey bridges to restore road connectivity severed by the floods, with components for the first 70-metre bridge reaching Nepal for deployment in the Betrawati area. India has provided three such bridges and pledged more as Nepal works to reconnect settlements cut off after floods washed away or damaged dozens of road and pedestrian crossings in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.
Article Summary: Nepal finance minister Swarnim Wagle will in New Delhi for a two-day visit from Thursday. Wagle is expected to meet finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal.
